verdict.reason: The commit renames the Literal class to Val while preserving backwards compatibility via Literal = Val. The three fail-to-pass tests exercise the new Val class definition, its registration in the type-checking logic in _t_eval, and the backwards-compatibility alias. This is a clear refactor that any capable engineer could implement from the problem statement.
verdict.title: Rename Literal to Val with backwards compatibility
verdict.statement:
In glom, the Literal spec class (which wraps a literal value to prevent it from being interpreted as a path/subspec) has been renamed to Val to better reflect its purpose. The old Literal name should still work for backwards compatibility.

The change involves renaming the Literal class to Val in glom/core.py. The Val class stores its value in self.value and implements glomit(target, scope) returning that value. The type check in _t_eval must recognize Val instances during path evaluation so they are not treated as dict keys. A backwards-compatibility alias Literal = Val should be added at the end of core.py. Both Val and Literal must be exported from glom/__init__.py. References in glom/matching.py should use Val instead of Literal.

To reproduce the issue before the fix: importing Val from glom raises ImportError, and using Val(...) in a spec causes a KeyError because Val is not recognized as a special spec type. After the fix, Val works as expected, and Literal remains available as an alias pointing to Val.
